title: Fall 1973 semester at Princeton
summary: He taught 14 students one-on-one at Princeton, designing his own program.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Just to refresh your memory, you got an invitation from Princeton from the Afro American Studies and Program of the Council of Humanities to come for a semester, and that was the Fall semester of 1973.
What were your ideas about what you ought to be doing at that time, and what did you do?
Well, prior to coming, I wasn't sure what I was going to be doing, but I was, you know, very pleased

that you allowed me the freedom to just come and really establish my own program, so to speak. I mean, because I didn't know what I was going to do; I had no sort of degree -- honorary or otherwise -- and I'd had just a small measure of formal training, and I had neither the time nor the inclination, and maybe not even the knowhow, I must add, to structure a curriculum.

But when I came, and had a meeting with the students, I think the first meeting we had, oh, 30-some students -- and I selected, I believe, 14 of them with whom I would work. On a one to one basis. I couldn't very well have worked with them all at the same time, because they were all at different levels of advancement, in addition to which they were all interested in certain aspects of music, you know -- one wanted to learn arranging, one wanted to study composition, one wanted to learn something else -- chord substitution; you know, they were all interested in different things.
So it worked out much better, I think -- it did certainly for me, and from what I understood from the students, they seemed to have been pleased with that effort.
Did you get some feeling of campus life over these 3 or 4 months?
Oh, I started feeling very, very much -- very academic.
You were already a pipe smoker.
So you fitted in very well.
Only thing, next time I come I'll have to get me some tweeds.
Tweeds, yes. Well, they wear all sorts of things now.
